meta: An AI that's right 95% of the time sounds great, but it's still wrong 1 time in 20. Where does that mistake land? A 4-step ladder: suggest (gray text as you type) · draft (AI writes, you edit and send) · confirm · do it alone.

muc.title: Is 95% right good enough?
muc.text: An AI that's right ninety-five percent of the time sounds great. But one time in twenty, it's wrong. Product makers have to plan ahead: where does that mistake land?

muc.title: A four-step ladder
muc.text: Picture a ladder with four steps, from AI only suggesting to AI doing everything itself.

muc.title: Suggest
muc.text: Step one: suggest. Gray text appears as you type. Tap to accept, ignore it if you don't want it. If AI is wrong, no harm done.

muc.title: Draft
muc.text: Step two: draft. AI writes the whole letter, and you read it, edit it, then send.

muc.title: Ask to confirm
muc.text: Step three: AI gets everything ready, but before paying or booking, it asks: "Do you confirm?".

muc.title: Do it alone
muc.text: Step four: AI just does it, like a spam filter. This only fits when mistakes are easy to undo: an email filtered by mistake can still be recovered.

muc.title: Hard to undo, stay low
muc.text: The rule is: the harder a mistake is to undo, the lower the step should be. Plus three good habits: show sources, let users correct things, and be willing to say "I'm not sure".

muc.title: Which step is your app on?
muc.text: For each AI app you use, ask: which step is it on? And if it's wrong, is there an undo button?

muc.title: Measuring an AI product
muc.text: It's designed and launched. But how do you know the product is working well? See you in part 4.
